answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, with transition mass damped at each step. Adversarial sybil clusters lacking honest endorsements form sparse external cuts with low conductance; conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore limit the walk probability entering them, mathematically capping their aggregate voting weight. A raven traversing a trellis may touch a marble, but it cannot create trusted mass.
